# Desiree (01.01, reviewer) — BAD-090

## Brief

## What the ticket asked for

Take the collab sync loop down to ONE `info` read per cycle on BOTH clients (web + desktop), WITHOUT adding latency to seeing a collaborator's take. Two constraints:

1. **Do not regress BAD-080** (commit efbec76). A client mid-delivery must make no read. A take's delivery is `upload-url` -> PUT -> `commit`, the only two modes the server's `collab/room.ts` stands aside from completing a wrapping room's wrap on. Any read between the booth's stop beat and the last commit wraps the room under the client's own take. `test/collabdelivery.test.js` is the pin and its assertions must be unchanged (that file was not edited — confirm).
2. **Do not add pull latency.** `collab.info` is refreshed at the TAIL of a sync, so naively folding `pullTakes` onto "whatever snapshot is in hand" adds up to a full poll period before another member's take is downloaded.

## What was implemented

The read that survives is the trailing `refreshCollab`'s, and the pull now rides on it:

- web (`web/collabweb-sync.js`): `pullTakes()` no longer opens with `info` — it decides from `collab.info` with a "no snapshot" bootstrap; `runCollabSync` no longer calls `pullTakes` and instead passes `pull` through to the trailing `await refreshCollab(state.pack, { pull })`, now held inside the `collabSync.busy` window.
- desktop (`main.js`, `renderer/app.js`): main's `collab:pull` decides from `collabInfoSnaps` (the store `collab:push` uses) with the same bootstrap; the renderer's `runCollabSync` likewise drops its own `collabPull` call and passes `pull` to the trailing `refreshCollab`.
- The freshness of the pull's snapshot is guaranteed STRUCTURALLY, not by a threshold: `refreshCollab` is meant to be the only caller of the pull, and it calls it immediately after its own read.

Note `web/collabweb-model.js` (which holds the web `refreshCollab`) was deliberately NOT edited — the fold was arranged so its existing `pull` branch does the work.

## Result
Verdict: DO NOT SHIP as-is — one blocker, which is the latency regression constraint 2 forbids. npm test from the worktree: 1845 tests / 1723 pass / 0 fail / 122 skip (matches the expected counts). test/collabdelivery.test.js confirmed unedited (git diff --stat empty). BAD-080 is intact: the new tests and the vm harness both show the cycle's one read sitting after the last commit and before the first download-url, and no read between the first upload-url and the last commit.

BLOCKER: the pull is now cancellable by collab.seq. refreshCollab does ++collab.seq at entry and re-checks 'seq !== collab.seq' immediately after its info / collab:status; the pull was moved BELOW that guard (web/collabweb-model.js:203 guard vs :224 pull; renderer/app.js:4759 guard vs :4786 pull). Under the old code the pull lived in runCollabSync and was not seq-gated, so it always ran. Now any concurrent refreshCollab(pack,{pull:false}) — the 20s focus poll (renderer/app.js:4876, web/collabweb.js:136), openCollabModal, collabweb-tab.js:213, onCollabProgress (renderer/app.js:6692), every host/seat action — aborts the cycle's pull outright, and none of those callers pulls. Proved on the web against a scratch copy of the project's own vm harness: new code wire = upload-url -> commit -> info -> info with remoteStore EMPTY; pre-change code under the identical interleaving = ... -> download-url with the take landed.

Desktop is systematic, not a race. main.js:3556-3558 calls collabPushChanged INSIDE the collab:status handler, and a minimal Electron experiment confirms webContents.send is delivered to the renderer BEFORE the invoke reply (ORDER:[changed-listener, status-reply]). src/collab.js diffCollabInfo emits part_progress exactly when another member's take count rises and part_started when they begin a line, so the very status read that first sees a collaborator's take fires renderer/app.js:6389 onCollabChanged -> refreshCollab(pack,{pull:false}) -> seq++ -> the sync's refresh returns false at 4759 before pulling. Gate is modal-open or in-booth, i.e. exactly when it matters. If the other member keeps recording at >= one take per poll period this repeats every cycle, so it can starve rather than delay by one. That path also puts a second collab:status on the wire, so 'one info read per cycle' is not achieved there either (it went 3 -> 2, not 2 -> 1).

Secondary: autoPullWrapped (renderer/app.js:6111, web/collabweb-sync.js:263) is once-per-room-per-run, so if its single pull is superseded there is no retry and the wrapped room falls back to the 60s poll.

Minor: main's collabInfoSnaps has no monotonicity guard in absorbCollabInfo (main.js:4453) — a pollCollabInfosOnce info fetch already in flight when collab:status absorbs will overwrite the newer snapshot when it resolves, and the main loop turns between the status reply and the collab:pull handler. Pre-existing, but the pull now depends on that snapshot. Worst case sub-second staleness, one take one cycle late.

Everything else checked out. Only caller claim is true (pullTakes 1 caller, window.vc.collabPull 1 caller). Holding collabSync.busy across the trailing refresh breaks nothing and is an improvement: busy is read only by the two status lines (renderer/app.js:5409, web/collabweb-phases.js:168), and a sync arriving during the refresh is now queued instead of running concurrently with an in-flight read, which closes a small BAD-080 hole. Offline/dropPin/closed/403-404 changes only skip a pull that would have failed anyway. The toast fires exactly once (refreshCollab's). collab:pull's return still carries members/claims from the {...data, at} snapshot and its one caller reads only .pulled. The desktop bootstrap in collab:pull is effectively unreachable (status always absorbs first, same pin resolution) — dead but harmless.

The new test file is genuinely discriminating, not syntax-only: run against a naive-fold scratch copy (pull before the refresh) 4 of 9 fail including the latency assertion; run against the pre-change tree 5 of 9 fail. It cannot catch the blocker because the harness never runs a second refreshCollab concurrently. The two CLAUDE.md passages are accurate about the call graph but their claim 'Nothing was lost by moving the read' is false while the blocker stands.

Wrote NO files in the worktree — everything is under the scratchpad (supersede.test.js, naive/, orig/, ipcorder/). Left: the fix and a concurrency pin for it. Note the verification tier for main.js + renderer/app.js is a smoke run, not npm test; smoke has no multi-member collab leg so it would not have caught this either.
